description: Contamination benchmarks (K6) and real-text corpora (K9) for the SSN pilot, each imported at a pinned revision before the build (dataworks_import_hf_dataset / import_slice; revisions are recorded at import, not here). Existence and licence checked on the Hugging Face Hub 2026-10-23; content fit not inspected (FTDD 11.6 'pilot open facts'). Real text is screened by every identifier rule set before use; a valid-format number found in it is dropped and counted (R-DLP.17).

contamination_benchmarks.note: how these are imported is an open fact (FTDD 11.6); resolve in 17.3

real_text_values.genre: non_english for fineweb-2 slices; the English corpora take a genre chosen per slice by the operator (web text is mixed-genre)
real_text_values.note: D70: each slice is inserted twice, as real_text_inserts says; kind and form are fixed per insert step

real_text_note: D70 settled the open question: real text carries positives (someones_identifier, with a framing phrase) at 40 % of the inserted real-text rows and negatives (other_number) at 60 %.

real_text_inserts.description: D70 (operator, 2026-10-25): real text carries positive examples too, not only negatives. Each real-text corpus is imported as TWO slices from disjoint data_files (dataworks_import_hf_dataset with data_files and max_rows = share x the corpus rows), so a positive and a negative insert never share a text. Each slice gets its own insert_element@1 step in real_text mode (definition '@input' or the resolved record, the vocabulary of plan.json, the rule-set pin of recipe.json) after one synth_identifier step (ssn_us, valid_share 1, delimiters [dash]; element_column its value). The positive share follows the generated plan's (about 43 % positive, D69). A positive insert puts a phrase from plan.json phrase_list before the element on every row (framing_phrase_share 1.0): web text does not present the number as anyone's SSN, so the phrase is what makes it one; a negative insert puts none, so 'SSN:' never precedes a number labelled no disclosure. Every inserted row is screened first like all real text (R-DLP.17).
